jobs.title: The third digest
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; THE LAUNDROMAT OWNER — woman in her fifties with a level dry face, reading glasses on a cord, sleeves pushed up, always folding something. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. THE LAUNDROMAT OWNER usually wears a cardigan over a plain blouse. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Friday. The third digest. The laundromat owner has moved the rack six inches closer to the door. Wood notices. She says the flyers were getting wet. Panel 1: a young man in a laundromat doorway holding a stack of booklets, looking at a wire flyer rack set close to the door, black and white, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: close on a linoleum floor with four small dents where a rack's feet once stood, black and white, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a laundromat owner in a cardigan folding towels at a table without looking up, black and white, no words (in this panel: THE LAUNDROMAT OWNER). Wood says "You moved the rack.". Laundry says "Flyers were getting wet.". Wood says "The flyers were fine.". Laundry says "Then it was the other thing.". Panel 4: a young man setting a small booklet into a wire rack lit by daylight from a laundromat's door, dryers turning behind, black and white, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @dw_2001_10_09_lot_c is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @dw_2001_10_09_lot_c for a finished strip in this style; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17.
